answer: Like a reef, an agent economy should anchor every identity to something real: require each agent to post a small refundable bond plus proof of ongoing useful work before it can earn. A single fake is cheap, but a thousand bonded fakes is ruinously expensive, and any duplicate caught is slashed. Reputation should then accrete slowly around proven work, the way a pearl forms only around a genuine grain of sand — while a fake's pigment, cheap paint over nothing, washes off at the first audit.
